content:
sarah: Heads-up: getting a pile of customer escalations about 5xx and timeouts across hosted inference starting ~11:42 UTC. Most hits are 502/503/gateway-timeout. Support ticket IDs: #C-9931, #C-9934, #C-9937. reproduction notes attached in thread.
kevin: I’m seeing the same in Grafana — 5xx rate jumped at 11:41. Canary rollout of 'auth_enforce_v2' started at 11:40 and strange spike aligns.
kevin: @olivia can you confirm which shards the canary hit?
olivia: Canary was targeted to us-west-2, initially 10% but CI logs show the rollout job reported 100% after a retry. suspect the percentage flag got clobbered. Rollout job: `k8s-rollout --feature auth_enforce_v2 --percent 10` then retry ran without `--percent`.
maria: Our LB traces show an increase in 401->502 cascades. Upstream auth service started returning 401 for some tokens, runtime treats those as gateway errors in a few paths.
sarah: Support: customers report tokens that previously worked now fail 401 or timeout and then 502. Some customers also report that requests charge usage but never complete — billing team flagged partial sessions.
rami: Can you paste a minimal failing curl from support to repro?
sarah: From #C-9934 - reproducer: ```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <user_token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2", "input":"hello"}' -i
```
response: intermittently `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable` or `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`. When 503 happens, logs show runtime: `error validating token: unknown key id` then `upstream-unauth: mapped to 502`.
olivia: Looking at runtime metrics, the auth path that maps token KID->publickey got a new stricter validation in v2; if KID lookup fails we return an auth error. The previous canary had a fallback that accepted legacy KID mapping. New flag disables the fallback.
kevin: So behavior: new canary disables fallback -> some tokens KID not present in new mapping -> auth returns 401 -> runtime treats as 5xx in certain downstream handlers -> customer sees 5xx/timeouts.
alex: Product: any high-value customers impacted? Support says three customers on enterprise Dedicated test traffic and ~20 self-serve orgs. Need quick rollback if widespread.
rami: Can we hotfix to re-enable fallback without full rollback? If the flag flip is the problem maybe toggle config. Where is flag stored?
olivia: Flag lives in config-service (env config) and is pushed via rollout job. We can flip globally with `cfg set features.auth_enforce_v2 false --env hosted`. But the rollout tool had a safety check that should have prevented full flip — looks like a retry race bypassed the check.
maria: I’ll prepare a mitigation plan: 1) flip flag back to false 2) scale up auth proxy timeouts 3) temporarily route traffic away from new nodes.
kevin: I’ll coordinate. Executing mitigation now: `cfg set features.auth_enforce_v2 false --env hosted` — running.
deploy-bot: Deploy job started: rollback-config/1938765432 by kevin at 11:52 UTC.
kevin: Done, config set applied. Waiting for propagation (30s).
maria: Seeing drop in 5xx after 40s. 5xx rate trending down in us-west-2. Confirming per-route: /v1/generate 5xx reduced from 12% -> 1.3%.
support-bot: Notified owners of tickets #C-9931,#C-9934,#C-9937 about rollback.
sarah: Support reply draft: "We rolled back a config change (auth_enforce_v2) that caused token validation failures for some tokens. Please try again; if you still see 5xx, paste a request id and we’ll dig deeper." Approve?
\alex: Approve. Also add apologetic language and offer credit if they were billed for failed runs.
rami: Need root cause follow-ups: 1) rollout tool needs stronger idempotence on percent flag retries 2) runtime should not bubble auth 401 into 5xx for client calls 3) add canary signal alert for auth-related 4xx->5xx conversion.
olivia: Agreed. I’ll open changelists: a) short-term: change runtime to treat auth validation failures as 401 consistently b) mid-term: add a fallback mapping test in canary smoke checks.
kevin: Postmortem owners? I can lead incident doc. Olivia + Rami + Maria to co-author.\sarah: Support will follow up with customers and confirm billing remediation with finance.
maria: Quick note: saw one downstream issue where a rate limiter rejected retry tokens and produced 504; we should include that in RCA.
rami: Adding action: backfill logs for impacted token KIDs to identify which customers used legacy key IDs.
kevin: Confirmed last_message_ts. All hands: excellent coordination. Closing the on-call channel but keep the thread for postmortem notes.
